channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Canadian Pacific Kansas City sees record February grain movement
item.description: Canadian Pacific Kansas City hit a new record for February movement of Canadian grain and grain products, moving 2.232 million tonnes in February 2026, the company reported on March 3.

item.title: Loblaw misses revenue estimate
item.description: Canadian retailer Loblaw says it has missed analysts’ estimates for fourth-quarter revenue, signalling consumers are turning cautious and more discerning.

item.title: CUSMA: a guide to the review and what it means for the agriculture sector
item.description: The upcoming Canada-Unites States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) review could set the tone for the future of Canadian agri-food trade. Here’s everything you need to know about CUSMA, the upcoming review process and what it could mean for the agriculture sector.

item.title: No way to segregate gene edited pigs Canadian Pork Council says as groups call for labeling
item.description: Canadian Pork Council says it supports bids to get public acceptance for pigs gene edited for resistance to PRRS as some consumer and agriculture groups call for mandatory labelling.

item.title: More canola, spring wheat likely to be seeded this spring
item.description: As spring planting approaches, farmers are busy planning which crops to seed this year and how much. With that, market thoughts have turned toward planted area projections, as Statistics Canada is set to issue its report on Thursday.

item.title: Canadian agriculture must build on the moment federal politicians say
item.description: Labour, investment, research and red tape as among the challenges the federal government and agriculture sector must address to increase productivity and competativeness politicians pointed to at the Canadian Federation of Agriculture (CFA) AGM.

item.title: East cashes in on climate funds
item.description: The On-Farm Climate Action Fund provides $300 million to farmers from coast to coast. A significant amount goes to Atlantic Canada, a region with minimal emissions from farming.

item.title: Drought may expand in U.S. Plains this year
item.description: SASKATOON — La Nina is rapidly fading and should be largely gone by spring, while El Nino is building but won’t be a force until autumn, says a weather forecaster. That means there will be neutral ENSO conditions for the upcoming growing season, said Brad Rippey, a U.S. Department of Agriculture meteorologist with the Office […] Read more

item.title: Loblaw, Ducks Unlimited partner on programs
item.description: Loblaw is contributing $400,000 this year to Ducks Unlimited Canada’s sustainable agriculture programs.

item.title: China has reduced tariffs on Canadian canola, peas, federal government confirms
item.description: China has suspended anti-discrimination tariffs on canola meal and peas until the end of the year and reduced tariffs on canola seed, Canada’s government confirmed today.
